title: Building a 1990s-style horror adventure in AGS with AI-assisted art, audio and code
author: lew82
selftext:
Hi everyone, I’m making Screemouth, a point-and-click horror adventure set in 1879, using Adventure Game Studio and extensive generative AI assistance.

One part of the process that might interest people here is the audio. I reviewed sound-effect candidates through several listening passes, left notes and approved revised takes before integration. The voices and effects then received a consistent Sound Blaster Pro-style treatment, while the music uses MT-32 synthesis rendered through Munt.

The music also follows story events rather than a fixed timeline. If the player skips dialogue, the cues still need to happen in the right place, alongside speech ducking, volume controls and save/restore behaviour.

AI has contributed extensively to artwork, voices, music, some effects and promotional material, as well as code and some story/dialogue. I direct the project, select and edit material, make design decisions and playtest the result. Generated content is included in the game; it is prepared during development rather than generated live while playing.

The project is in development, with a free public demo planned. [Screenshots and the opening video are here](https://lew82.itch.io/screemouth).

For anyone using a similar workflow, how are you keeping the art and audio consistent as individual assets go through revisions? I’d be interested in comparing notes.

Cheers,  
Lew
